initialInstallPackageNotes: Official procedure (confirmed independently twice -- once via the cyberknight777.dev/DroidWin guide pattern, once directly by the device owner from the official download page): boot to fastbootd ('adb reboot fastboot'), flash the initial-install package with 'fastboot --skip-reboot update <package>.zip', then 'fastboot reboot recovery' and 'adb sideload <rom>.zip'. The device owner's locally downloaded file is named approximately 'infinity_gms_initial_install...zip'. A dedicated 2026-10-10 research pass (WebFetch on the official download page and the cyberknight777.dev instructions page -- both DNS-blocked in this sandbox as before; plus several WebSearch queries, one of which surfaced a real indexed snippet of the cyberknight777.dev guide itself naming its initial-install filename convention for another ROM family, e.g. 'yaap_banshee_cancunf_initial_install.zip') found NO MD5/SHA-256/SHA-1 or checksum manifest published anywhere for this specific package type, for any ROM on that guide, cancunf or otherwise. android-info.txt itself (the manifest 'fastboot update' reads) carries no checksum field by AOSP's own format -- only 'require board='. CHECKSUM_UNAVAILABLE for this package is therefore now Warning-severity (non-blocking) rather than Blocking: its identity is instead verified by its declared required-board match against the device profile's codename (RomValidationService.CheckDeclaredDeviceCompatibility), which still blocks unconditionally on a mismatch. If an official checksum is ever found or published, add it to knownOfficialInitialInstallChecksums below and it will be enforced exactly as strictly as the ROM package's checksums are.
dataFormatNotes: The official cancunf guide's clean-install procedure includes a Recovery data format step (fastboot -w) before sideloading the ROM. Moving from stock Motorola firmware to an AOSP-derived custom ROM for the first time also independently requires this due to filesystem/encryption differences.
kernelSuNotes: KernelSU officially supports GKI 2.0 kernels (5.10+) with a matching KMI; a non-GKI or older kernel needs a manually built KernelSU kernel, which this app will not attempt to source or flash blindly. Whether the Infinity-X 3.12 cancunf build ships a KernelSU-enabled kernel out of the box has not been confirmed -- VERIFY_KERNELSU_COMPATIBILITY checks the installed kernel's 'uname -r' string and the boot image itself (see KernelSuCompatibilityChecker) rather than assuming compatibility from the ROM's name or Android version. This is deliberately independent of whether KernelSU Manager is merely installed -- see RootDetector/RootSolutionType for why that alone never proves kernel integration.

citations.title: Dedicated research pass: does an official checksum exist for the Initial Install package? (2026-10-10)
citations.note: Re-attempted WebFetch on both https://projectinfinity-x.com/downloads/cancunf and https://cyberknight777.dev/instructions/cancunf/ -- both still DNS-blocked from this sandbox, unchanged from earlier. Four separate WebSearch queries targeting the initial-install package specifically (its exact approximate filename, general Infinity-X checksum-requirement policy for this package type, Motorola cancunf firmware-package checksum conventions, and cyberknight777's GitHub device trees) found no MD5/SHA-256/SHA-1 or checksum manifest for it anywhere, for any ROM family, not just Infinity-X -- including in a real indexed snippet of the cyberknight777.dev guide's own text (which named a different ROM's initial-install filename convention but no checksum). One search result speculated cancunf might be a different, unrelated device codename; that is a search-summarizer error, not a finding -- this session has independently confirmed cancunf is the Motorola Moto G54/G64 5G via the device profile's own citations and is not revised here. Conclusion: no authoritative checksum for this package type was ever found to exist, so CHECKSUM_UNAVAILABLE for it was downgraded to non-blocking (see initialInstallPackageNotes) rather than left as an unclosable block.
